newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares fall, seen up on Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares fall, seen up on Wednesday.

text.p: Polish shares fell 0.8 percent on Tuesday after a six-session surge but analysts said the dominant buying after price fixing signalled a rebound on Wednesday.
But they were divided on the degree to which the 14.5-percent surge fuelled by foreign buying would continue as the nature of the demand was not yet clear.

"Foreign capital has been flowing in strongly -- the question is whether its character is long-term or speculative. But it seems what's happening with Bank Slaski suggests it can be pretty long-term," said Czeslaw Pospieszynski, an analyst at Polish Investment Bank (PBI) brokerage.
Bank Slaski rose 3.9 percent on Tuesday in heavy trade, achieving a seven-session 36-percent surge in high turnovers.
But some analysts said macroeconomic uncertainties would cap bourse growth.

"I don't think it's a long-term tendency -- it was too quick a rebound and seems more speculative....The economy must stabilise, for example the foreign trade deficit must improve and flood loans could increase cash in circulation," said Pawel Demczuk, a trader at Wood & Company.

The main market's all-share WIG index fell 0.8 percent to 17,166.5 and turnover fell 11.4 percent to 273.3 million zlotys ($78.2 million) on both markets. Gainers led losers by 79 to 22 with 10 stocks flat.
Analysts said Tuesday's biggest loser, electrode maker ZEW SA, which fell 10 percent and extended Monday's 5.2-percent drop after a flood suspension, should begin to slow its fall.
Banks Gdanski and Amerbank, down 8.9 percent and five percent, hit corrections on Tuesday in light trade.
